findings.title: The retry-count delete is not limited to SMS reminders.
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so this SMS cron deletes every `workflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, including email and WhatsApp ones. This PR only increments `retryCount` here, but the column is now on the shared model. Once another scheduler (email, WhatsApp) starts counting retries, this job will silently delete those reminders before they are sent. Move `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the `OR`, or add it to both branches.

findings.title: If the retry update in the catch block throws, the whole cron run stops.
findings.body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside `catch` has no error handling of its own. If it throws, the error escapes the `for` loop and the handler returns a 500. That happens when the reminder row was deleted in the meantime (P2025, for example when the booking was cancelled while this run was in progress) or when the database has a transient error. Every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is then skipped for this run. Before this change the catch only logged, so one bad reminder could not stop the batch. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany` with the id, which does not throw when no row matches.
